cleanIntro: The INTEGRA 15-22 is a complete upper receiver for the M&P 15-22 rifle with the suppressor built onto a 17.5 inch barrel. The G-CORE baffle stack is pinned and welded to the barrel; the only part that comes off is the aluminium outer tube, which unscrews counterclockwise. Gemtech wants it opened and cleaned every 250 rounds, and cleaned once before first use. It is rated for .22 Long Rifle only, it is DRY ONLY, it is not full-auto rated, and 60 grain subsonic and .22 shotshell are both ruled out. Fitting the upper to the lower, and everything about the rifle itself, comes from the M&P 15-22 manual. Deep Clean is Gemtech's method for build-up that a brush will not shift.

steps.title: Magazine out, chamber and action cleared by hand
steps.action: Never adjust or clean the INTEGRA upper on a loaded rifle. Take the magazine out first, then look into the chamber AND check it with a finger, and clear the action. Gemtech counts a firearm as unloaded only when the action is open, the magazine is out, and you have seen that the chamber is empty.
steps.prose: A .22 case is small and easy to miss in a chamber. Look, then feel.
steps.quote: WARNING: Never ATTEMPT TO ADJUST OR CLEAN a suppressed UPPER RECEIVER ON a loaded firearm. First remove the magazine from the FIREARM. Second, visually and manually check and clear the chamber and action OF AMMUNITION.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Attaching a Suppressed Upper Receiver, p.9

steps.title: The rifle's own manual does the rifle
steps.action: Get the M&P 15-22 rifle manual out and keep it beside this one. Gemtech says the INTEGRA upper goes on and comes off the lower exactly as any M&P 15-22 upper does, and sends you to that manual for it. This book covers the suppressed barrel: its ammunition limits and cleaning it.
steps.prose: Two books, two jobs. Separating the upper from the lower, the bolt and the rest of the rifle all come from the rifle's manual.
steps.quote: Installation of the INTEGRA® 15-22 upper is done in the same manner as with any M&P® 15-22 rifle. Follow the procedure as detailed in the M&P® 15-22 Safety & Instruction manual.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Mounting the INTEGRA 15-22 Upper on an M&P 15-22 Lower Receiver, p.18

steps.title: .22 LR only — no 60 grain subsonic, no shotshell
steps.action: Check what it has been fed. The INTEGRA 15-22 is chambered for .22 Long Rifle — subsonic, standard or high velocity — and is not full-auto rated. Gemtech rules out 60 grain subsonic .22 LR, which can fail to stabilise and yaw into the suppressor's internals, and it rules out .22 shotshell entirely. No tracer and no frangible ammunition through any Gemtech suppressor either.
steps.prose: If you have been running 60 grain subsonics, Gemtech treats any damage as your risk and the warranty as void.
steps.quote: WARNING: NEVER USE 22 SHOTSHELL AMMUNITION IN THE INTEGRA 15-22 SUPPRESSED UPPER.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Ammunition, p.8
steps.warn: WARNING: Do not use 60 gr. Subsonic 22LR ammunition in GEMTECH INTEGRA 15-22 Suppressed UPPER.

steps.title: Let it cool before you touch it
steps.action: Let the suppressed barrel cool before you handle it. Gemtech puts it past 900 degrees F in use. If it has to be handled hot, use a glove or suppressor sock made for extreme heat, and keep it away from anything that can burn.
steps.prose: A hot suppressor does not look hot. Decide where it will rest before you start shooting.
steps.quote: WARNING: THE SUPPRESSED BARREL OR UPPER RECEIVER CAN BECOME DANGEROUSLY HOT WITH USAGE (> 900° F) WHICH COULD CAUSE SEVERE SKIN BURN ON CONTACT OR COULD IGNITE FLAMMABLE MATERIALS OR VAPORS IN THE ENVIRONMENT.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Removing a Suppressed Upper Receiver, p.9

steps.title: Outer tube off, counterclockwise
steps.action: Twist the outer tube counterclockwise to unscrew it off the suppressed barrel. That exposes the G-CORE baffle stack on the barrel. Gemtech's interval for this whole maintenance process is every 250 rounds.
steps.prose: On a .22, 250 rounds is one range trip. Keeping to it is also what keeps the tube easy to get off next time.
steps.aside: For optimal performance and ease of disassembly, perform the maintenance process listed below every 250 rounds.
steps.quote: Remove outer tube by twisting counter clockwise.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Maintenance, p.18

steps.title: The G-CORE stays on the barrel
steps.action: Do not try to take the G-CORE off the barrel. It is pinned and welded there permanently; trying to remove it damages it, and Gemtech says removing it is illegal. You clean it where it sits.
steps.prose: The core and barrel are one part as far as you are concerned.
steps.quote: CAUTION: The inner G-CORE® is permanently pinned and welded to the barrel. DO NOT attempt to remove the G-CORE® from the barrel. Damage will result.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Maintenance, p.18
steps.warn: It is also illegal to remove the G-CORE® from the barrel.

steps.title: G-CORE: nylon brush and non-marring picks, with CLP
steps.action: Clean the deposits and debris off the G-CORE with a nylon brush and non-marring picks. Gemtech recommends CLP as the cleaner. A brass brush or a metal pick is a last resort, only for stubborn lead and carbon the non-marring tools will not move.
steps.prose: Metal tools shorten the life of the core. Keeping to the 250-round interval is what keeps you from needing them.
steps.caution: Take care when using metal tools as their use can damage suppressor components and decrease their useful service life.
steps.aside: We recommend using a CLP (Cleaner, Lubricant, Preservative) to clean.
steps.quote: When cleaning suppressor internal components use a nylon brush and non-marring cleaning pics to remove deposits and debris.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Maintenance, p.19

steps.title: Inside of the outer tube
steps.action: Soak a nylon bore brush or a mop in CLP and run it through the outer tube to get the debris out. If the build-up will not come out with the brush, Deep Clean has Gemtech's method for it.
steps.prose: Clean the tube's threads as well — they have to be clean before it goes back on.
steps.quote: To clean the inside of the suppressor tube soak a nylon bore brush or mop in CLP and run it through the tube to remove debris.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Maintenance, p.19

steps.title: Bore and chamber
steps.action: Clean the firing residue out of the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent. Finish with a dry cotton patch through the bore to take out the residue and the solvent.
steps.prose: Count your patches out. A patch left in the barrel or the suppressor is a bore obstruction.
steps.aside: Finish the bore cleaning process by running a dry cotton cloth patch through the bore to remove residue and solvent.
steps.quote: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chamber using a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Cleaning the INTEGRA 15-22 Suppressed Upper, p.20

steps.title: Everything dry before the tube goes back
steps.action: Before the tube goes back on, the tube, the core and the threads must be dry and wiped clean of excess cleaner and debris. The INTEGRA 15-22 is a DRY ONLY suppressor.
steps.prose: If cleaner got inside, blow it dry with compressed air. Liquid left in a suppressor raises the pressure when you fire and can damage it.
steps.quote: Before reassembly the tube, core, and threaded surfaces must be dry, and wiped clean of all excess cleaner and debris.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Maintenance, p.19

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have the outer tube off and the G-CORE, the tube and the bore cleaned and dry. That is all the disassembly Gemtech publishes; anything else goes to Gemtech. Deep Clean covers stubborn build-up and putting the tube back on.
steps.prose: Write the date and round count in the maintenance log at the back of the book.
steps.quote: No other disassembly of the suppressor is necessary.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Cleaning a Suppressed Upper Receiver, p.11

deepSteps.title: Use the core to break off stubborn build-up
deepSteps.action: If lead and carbon build-up stays in the tube, Gemtech's method is to use the core itself. Coat the inside of the tube with CLP, let it sit a few minutes, then run the tube on and off the core 15 to 20 times until it feels more like the intended slip fit.
deepSteps.prose: The slip-fit feel is the test. A tube that still drags on the core has fouling left in it.
deepSteps.aside: If lead/carbon build up persists, the core can be used to break off the buildup.
deepSteps.quote: Coat the inside of the tube with CLP, let it sit for a few minutes then run the tube on and off of the core 15-20 times until it feels more like the intended slip fit.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Maintenance, p.19

deepSteps.title: Metal tools only as a last resort
deepSteps.action: For lead and carbon on the core that nylon and non-marring tools will not move, a brass brush or metal pick may be used — as a last resort only. Work carefully: metal tools damage suppressor components and shorten their life.
deepSteps.prose: If you find yourself reaching for metal often, clean more often.
deepSteps.quote: Metal hand tools like a brass brush and metal cleaning pick can be used only as a last resort to remove stubborn lead and carbon deposits on internal components that are not removed by non-marring tools.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Maintenance, p.19

deepSteps.title: Dry, then the tube back on hand tight
deepSteps.action: With the tube, core and threads dry and wiped clean, screw the tube back onto the suppressed barrel. Hand tight only — no wrench.
deepSteps.prose: Over-tightening makes the next removal harder and risks the tube. Tube damage on a registered suppressor means a new suppressor.
deepSteps.quote: Install the tube back on to the suppressed barrel- HAND TIGHTEN ONLY.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Maintenance, p.19

deepSteps.title: Protect the tube: it cannot be replaced
deepSteps.action: Treat the outer tube with care at every step. Gemtech notes that a damaged tube cannot take the serial number onto a new one, so tube damage means a new suppressor. Anything beyond the tube-off clean goes back to Gemtech for service.
deepSteps.prose: No vice on the tube, no pipe wrench, and watch M-LOK screws around the recessed suppressor body: Gemtech warns that screws touching the tube may damage it.
deepSteps.quote: NOTE: BATFE prohibits transferring the serial number to a new outer tube in the case of damage to the tube. Tube damage will require a new suppressor.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual For: INTEGRA® 15-22 Suppressed Upper Receiver — p/n 3013199 REV: INTEGRA1522-030120 — Gemtech Repair Policy, p.14

cleaning.name: G-CORE
tasks: Interval: every 250 rounds, and once before first use
Nylon brush, non-marring picks and CLP
Brass brush or metal pick only as a last resort
Never try to remove the G-CORE from the barrel

cleaning.name: OUTER TUBE
tasks: Nylon bore brush or mop soaked in CLP run through the tube
Stubborn build-up: coat with CLP, wait, run the tube on and off the core 15-20 times

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Dry cotton patch through the bore to finish
No patch left in the barrel or suppressor

cleaning.name: BEFORE REASSEMBLY
tasks: Tube, core and threads dry and wiped clean
Any cleaner inside: blow dry with compressed air
Exterior wiped with a non-abrasive cloth

reassembly: Check that the tube, the core and every threaded surface are dry and wiped clean.
Screw the outer tube back onto the suppressed barrel clockwise, hand tight only.
Fit the upper to the M&P 15-22 lower exactly as the M&P 15-22 rifle manual describes.
Record the date and round count in the maintenance log.
fncheck: With the rifle unloaded and the magazine out, confirm the outer tube is screwed fully home hand tight and has not loosened, and that the upper is fitted to the lower as the M&P 15-22 manual describes. Check that the bore and the suppressor are clear of any obstruction, including a lost patch, before firing; Gemtech warns that an improperly installed suppressed upper can cause a baffle strike.
